page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1ne.4xlarge is an instance type within the Big Data family, configured for high-density local disk storage and distributed processing. Virtualized on KVM, the instance delivers 16 vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores on an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The x86_64 CPU features dedicated hardware allocation, 33 MB of L3 cache, and instruction support including AVX, AVX-512F, BMI2, ADX, and AES. Memory allocation is set at 64.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, and the network interface provides a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps. Graphical acceleration is absent.

A key architectural aspect of the ecs.d1ne.4xlarge is its bundled local storage array, offering 47,244 GB of physical hard disk drive (HDD) capacity. In CPU-centric testing, the instance exhibits typical Broadwell-era behavior with single-threaded results falling into lower percentiles, such as a Geekbench single-core score of 963.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 19.12 GB/sec. When parallelized across all 16 vCPUs, throughput shifts into average ranges, demonstrated by a Geekbench multi-core score of 5908.0, a PassMark CPU score of 12,996.41, and 11.3 million operations per second on Redis SET operations.

The qualitative profile of this server prioritizes raw bulk storage density over peak single-thread execution or low-latency solid-state storage. Given its massive spinning-disk capacity, 12 Gbps network baseline, and multithreaded capacity, the ecs.d1ne.4xlarge is positioned for MapReduce distributed computing clusters, Hadoop nodes, centralized log aggregation, large-scale ETL data ingestion pipelines, and long-term storage-heavy database deployments.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1ne.4xlarge is a big data server instance powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor operating at 2.5 GHz on KVM virtualization. The configuration delivers 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores, 64.0 GB of system memory, and a 12 Gbps baseline network capacity, without hardware GPU acceleration. A defining element of this configuration is its bundled local storage array, supplying 47,244 GB of HDD capacity. In benchmark evaluations, the server exhibits modest single-thread metrics alongside solid average multi-threaded throughput, registering 11,778.16 in stress-ng multi-core tests and 11.3 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. This hardware profile trades single-core speed and solid-state latency for massive sequential data volume and stable multi-core processing, making it well matched for distributed Hadoop clusters, data lake ingestion, ETL batch jobs, and log repository workloads.
